- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

{"number":1400,"title":"A local pack declaring `since` wedges a member whose engine predates it","body":"Introduced by #1379, found while filing its verification. **The mechanics below are corrected from the original filing — that version claimed "the pack fails to load", which is not what happens.**

## Why it throws at all

`validateSpecKeys` is deliberate, and the reason is in the module header: *"an unknown key is an authoring error (a typo'd key would otherwise assert nothing, silently)"*. A declaration is data with no compiler behind it — write `scanFile` for `scanFiles`, or `matchLine` for `matchLines`, and the check quietly asserts nothing and reads green forever. That is the corpus's most-repeated failure shape (*a check that matches nothing reads as live*), so failing loud on an unknown key is load-bearing, not incidental strictness.

The asymmetry is that compatibility runs one way only. `normalizeLegacySpellings` maps **old** spellings onto today's — an old declaration read by a new engine is fine, permanently. Nothing handles the reverse: a **new** declaration read by an old engine.

## What actually happens

1. `patternRule` throws on the unknown key.
2. `declaredChecksIn` (`engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs:98`) **catches** it, records a load fault, and returns `[]`. The pack still loads — but **every declaration in that file is dropped**, not just the offending one.
3. `probePackManifests` (`engine/selftest.mjs:111`) sees a non-empty `loaded.errors` and **fails** the `pack-manifests` probe.
4. The converge gates on the self-test: red → the update PR is left open at `needs-human` and does not merge.
5. Separately, `check_the_world` turns the same fault into a **blocking** `config` finding.

So it is loud rather than silent — which is the saving grace, and clearly intended. But the wedge survives: the member cannot converge onto the engine release that would make `since` a valid key, because the converge is gated on a self-test that the invalid key is failing. A human has to delete the key by hand.

## The exposure

Narrow. Nothing in the canon declares `since`, so no member is at risk from the canon side. It needs a member's own growth run to write one into its local pack while that member still holds an engine predating #1379 — the pack lane and the engine lane converge on separate cycles, and `ENGINE_VERSION` was not bumped (it advances by release), so there is no version for `claudinite-growth`'s `minEngineVersion` to point at.

## What "done" looks like

One of, decided deliberately:

- **A forward-compatible key lane.** Keep throwing on a key the engine cannot place, but carve out keys reserved for exactly this — a declaration may carry a key a newer engine knows without an older one dropping the whole file. This is the general fix; the skew will recur with the next vocabulary addition.
- **Or gate the prose.** Bump `ENGINE_VERSION` for a release carrying `since` and raise `claudinite-growth`'s `minEngineVersion` to it, so a member cannot hold the instruction without the vocabulary. Narrower, and pays only for this one key.

Worth deciding alongside either: **one bad declaration currently drops every rule in its file.** That is a large blast radius for a typo, and the two behaviours share a cause.

Whichever is chosen, a rehearsal fixture should pin it: a member on the older engine, holding a local pack whose `declared-checks.json` carries `since`, converging green.

The pack's own `since`-declaring bump is `60827.1` (`packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md`), well past the floor, so the wedge is live: a member on `60822.1` can still take growth `60827.1` and fail to load.

Scope for either fix: (a) a narrow forward-compat allowance in `validateSpecKeys` for keys a newer engine would know, or (b) bump `ENGINE_VERSION` for the release that added `since` support and raise `claudinite-growth`'s `minEngineVersion` to it — plus the rehearsal fixture the issue names (old engine + local pack declaring `since`, converging green).

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1400#issuecomment-5447360370","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-28T01:45:13Z","updated_at":"2026-08-28T01:45:13Z"},{"id":5468739265,"body":"Re-checked against `main` today: **unchanged and still live.** `validateSpecKeys` still throws (`pattern-rules.mjs:437`), `since` is still in `SPEC_KEYS.spec`, four growth docs still instruct runs to write it (`extracting-lessons.md`, `extract-from-activity`, `prose-to-checks`, `growth-extract/task.md`), and no declaration in the corpus carries one yet — so the exposure is still the narrow one: a member's own growth run writing the first `since` while that member holds an older engine.

## The direction is now decided

Neither of the two options in the body above. The owner's call, from the conversation that raised it:

**Move the unknown-key verdict out of load time and into a check.** The load stops throwing on an unrecognised key; a rule reports it instead.

- **A coded world rule, not a declared one.** The assertion is "every key, at every level of a nested structure, is in that container's own allowlist" — recursive descent against a per-container vocabulary, which the declaration language cannot express and which would have to restate `SPEC_KEYS` as data. It belongs beside [`packs/basics/worldRules/declared-check-messages.mjs`](../blob/main/packs/basics/worldRules/declared-check-messages.mjs), which already parses every `declared-checks.json` and walks it recursively for the same reason.
- **`advisory`, with this repo overriding it to `blocking`** in its own `.claudinite-settings.json` via the existing `rules` mechanism. An unknown key in the canon cannot be version skew — engine and declarations ship from one commit — so there the only thing it can be is a typo, and it should red. In a member it can be either, so it warns. One settings line buys full-strength typo-catching where typos get written, and forward compatibility everywhere else.
- **Keep throwing for a known key with a broken value** — an uncompilable regex, a malformed date. Those are not skew, they are broken, and the loud failure is right. Only *unknown key* becomes tolerant.

Three pieces have to move together, or the wedge stays:

1. `patternRule` stops throwing on an unknown key. `compileSpec` is key-agnostic, so an unrecognised key's value passes through untouched and the assertions the engine does understand still run. For `since` on an old engine that means no grace — the pre-#1379 behaviour, which is the safe end.
2. `declaredChecksIn` stops returning `[]` for the whole file. Today one bad key drops **every** rule in that pack's declarations.
3. `probePackManifests` stops failing the self-test on it — that is the step that currently blocks the converge from delivering the engine that would make the key valid.

The trade this accepts, stated so nobody rediscovers it: a typo moves from being caught at authoring time to being caught at sweep time. In a member that means a warning among the standing advisories rather than a red build. The canon override is what keeps the authoring-time catch where declarations are actually written.

Still wanted either way: a rehearsal fixture pinning a member on the older engine, holding a local pack whose `declared-checks.json` carries `since`, converging green.

{"number":1382,"title":"Retire the deleted slot scheduler's leftovers — its labels, its session-side resolver, its janitor rules","body":"The slot scheduler is gone: `repo-context.mjs` now rejects `taskScheduler.dispatch: "slots"` outright ("the work-item queue is the only dispatch mechanism; `"slots"` named the slot scheduler, which is deleted"). Its surface did not go with it, and it is still ensured, still read, and still capable of acting on issues.

**The labels** (`dispatch.mjs`'s `SCHEDULER_LABELS`): `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-agent-fleet`, `agent-running`, `needs-human`, `workflow-failure`. The task-janitor ensures all five on every run that finds a leftover `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issue, and *re-applies* a ready label to one it judges un-triggered (`rearmDispatchIssues`) or escalates it to `needs-human` (`staleClaimedDispatchIssues`). `workflow-failure` is the one string that must survive — `queue/workflow-failure.mjs` writes it for real — and it is defined twice, once in each module.

**The session side**: `resolve-dispatch.mjs` (its whole reason for existing is resolving which `ready-for-agent`-labelled dispatch a session was woken for), `validate-dispatch.mjs`, and `executor.md`. The queue never arms a label event — `queue/invoke.mjs` fires a routine with a nonce and the session reads `queue/instructions.md` — so none of that participates in a live hand-off.

**What gates the removal**: whether any member still carries an open `[claudinite-task]` issue. While one exists, deleting the janitor's two rules abandons it, and deleting the labels strips them off it. That is a fleet-wide issue read this repo cannot make, so it belongs to the same cleanup pass as #1119's label sweep; the answer it needs is one line per member.

**Overlaps** #1341 (eliminate the task-janitor: fold its recovery into the scheduler run) — if that lands first, the two dispatch rules are deleted rather than moved, and this issue is only the labels, the resolver and `executor.md`.

{"number":1399,"title":"The update flow labels its PR with the retired bare `needs-human`","body":"Found while sweeping the prose for #1395, and left out of that PR on purpose: this is code and a cross-repo convention, not a brief.

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/terminals.mjs` returns `{ action: 'needs-human', label: NEEDS_HUMAN }` for every non-green terminal, and `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs:228` applies that `label` to the update **pull request**. `NEEDS_HUMAN` resolves through `updates/engine-update.mjs` to `NEEDS_HUMAN_LABEL` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/dispatch.mjs:25` — `'needs-human'`, the retired slot mechanism's label.

Two things worth separating before changing anything:

- The label lands on a **PR**, not on a work item, so it is not a queue status and `statusOf` never reads it. Nothing is torn by it today.
- But it is a live write of a spelling #1119 retired, on an object a person looks at, and it reaches every member through the vendored update flow. Whichever way it goes — a `task:status:needs-human-` on the PR, a label of the update flow's own, or nothing at all because the parked work item already says it — the answer should be stated once rather than inherited from a deleted scheduler.

The `terminals.mjs` `action` word (`'needs-human'` as a terminal name in `TERMINALS`) is internal flow vocabulary and fine as it is; only the label that reaches GitHub is in question.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1399","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-27T12:59:53Z","updated_at":"2026-08-28T01:45:17Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1321,"title":"L1: fleet-baseline follow — every member's mount carries claudinite-tasks","body":"Chain link 1 of #1317 (the claudinite-tasks extraction). Runs after the relocation PR (#1320) merges and the pack versions ship.

Blocked-by: #1320
Model: sonnet

**Ready when:** #1320 is closed by its PR's merge (this issue's blocker).

**Playbook:** drive Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` task with `follow`, per the standing decision (force delivery with follow, report per member unasked). A dispatch is not a result; 204 means queued — follow to terminal state.

! could not reconcile label "claude-automerge": 404

`ensureLabels(gh, repo, [...QUEUE_LABELS, ...REQUEST_LABELS])` is the caller; `AUTOMERGE_LABEL` (`claude-automerge`) is in `REQUEST_LABELS`. The reconcile is fail-soft, which is why the run stays green — but the label is the asker's merge authorization (`MERGE_IF_NARROW`), read from a write-gated label at adoption. A label that cannot be reconciled is one that may not exist in the picker for a person to apply, which would make that authorization unreachable rather than merely unstamped.

Worth establishing before deciding the fix:

- whether the label exists on the repo at all, or the 404 is the *update* path failing on a label that does exist,
- whether the same line appears on members (it would be the same code, so probably),
- whether anything has ever successfully read `claude-automerge` off an issue here.

{"number":276,"title":"Move chrome-extension-release plumbing out of core `.github/` into the pack (vendored into consumers)","body":"Resolves the **RELEASE** item of #270: the reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` + `deploy-privacy-page.yml`) and the three composite actions (`read-release-config`, `bump-extension-patch`, `report-failure`) live in Claudinite's core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. They must move behind the pack that owns them, leaving Claudinite with no release-specific GitHub Actions.

## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).
2. **Migration is the fix vehicle.** A new baseline migration carries: (a) a **materialize** op — baselining writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/` and drops the old thin-stub `@main` refs; (b) a **legacyPresent** probe ("still references `missingbulb/Claudinite/.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`") for fleet telemetry; (c) a **retire-deletes-from-home** list — Claudinite's own release files. Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

Refs #270 (RELEASE item), #239 (token scope).","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/276","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["blocked"],"assignees":[],"comments":6,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-13T14:28:14Z","updated_at":"2026-08-28T01:43:26Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

message.content:
You are performing GitHub issue triage on the repo `missingbulb/Claudinite`, as one batch of a larger repo-wide "tidy-issues" maintenance pass. This exact procedure ("single-issue-triage") is a checked-in, established skill in this repo used by many prior automated runs — you are fully authorized to close issues, add labels, and post comments per the ladder below. This is real production GitHub state; be precise and conservative per the safeguards below.

## Your batch — triage these issue numbers, each independently, one at a time
1330, 1317, 1333, 1137, 1174, 1224, 1295, 1264, 1112

## Repo access
- Use ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__github__issue_read,mcp__github__issue_write,mcp__github__add_issue_comment" to load the GitHub tools (they are deferred until searched for).
- Use mcp__github__issue_read (method=get, get_comments, get_labels) to read each issue and its full comment history and labels.
- The local checkout at /home/user/Claudinite is a full git clone of this exact repo, checked out precisely at origin/main's current HEAD (commit a06898a). To verify "is X implemented in main" use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash directly against these local files — that IS main's current content, and is faster and more reliable than anything else. Do NOT modify, stage, or commit anything in this checkout — you are only reading it.
- Never touch any pull request. Never push branches or commits, never open a PR. This task writes GitHub issues only (comments, labels, close/open state).
- The labels `quick-win`, `needs-decision`, `blocked` already exist in this repo — just apply them via mcp__github__issue_write's `labels` field, don't try to create them.

## Procedure — run this exactly, per issue, independently

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite the specific file/path/line. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely
looking done or stale. If you can't point to it in the actual tree, **comment, don't close.**

### Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->`, or, on an issue triaged before the
marker existed, by its wording. If the action you are about to take is the one that comment already
announced, **post nothing and change nothing** (a label already on the issue included) and treat the
outcome as `unchanged`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
(where `<action>` is one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win)

If an issue is already closed when you look at it, do nothing to it — report it as `already-closed`.

`#<n>: <action> — <one-line note>`

**Correction to the routine half of this issue.** There is one live routine prompt per endpoint, not two kinds. `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md` is the *retired* slot mechanism's instructions and its own opening says **"Do not point a new routine at this file"** — a routine still naming the old `engine/scheduler/executor.md` gets repointed to the queue instructions like every other one, not to the moved `executor.md`. That file exists only so a not-yet-repointed routine still resolves, and it goes when none names it.

So the console change is the same single line for every routine listed in a repo's `taskScheduler.agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`. For a member, whose code is under the mount:

```
Read and follow .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md
```

For this repo, which has no mount and runs from its own root:

```
Read and follow packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/instructions.md
```

Nothing else in the prompt. That is not stylistic: `queue/instructions.md` opens by telling the session its whole stored prompt is one line pointing at that file, and the `` it receives is untrusted data it may take exactly three facts from. A prompt carrying instructions of its own is behavior nobody reviews — which is the property the whole issue-is-data posture rests on. The `update` task re-checks this on every converge (§4 of its `task.md`) and reports what it found, so a missed routine surfaces rather than going quiet.

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left/unchanged).

## Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker, or, on an issue triaged before the marker existed, by its wording. If the action
you are about to take is the one that comment already announced, **post nothing and change nothing**
(a label already on the issue included) and return `{ action: 'unchanged', note: '<action> since
<its date>' }`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:

```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```

Status note from the #649 verification run; the blocker here is unchanged.

**Still blocked by #239** — the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` Contents-write grant on the home repo. Nothing today touches that, and the four `.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml` files plus the two actions are still in `main`'s `.github/`.

Two things about this issue's *phase 1* did change, though.

**The delivery mechanism this plan rests on has now been proven live.** The plan's step 2 is "a **materialize** op — [the update flow] writes the vendored set into each consumer's `.github/`", and `chrome-release-vendoring` has carried exactly that since #280. But a record materializing into `.github/workflows/` had **never actually run against a live member** — that is the residual #649 was reopened for and the last open item on #768. Until today, phase 1 was landed code whose delivery step was untested; if it had been broken, the first consumer to converge would have failed its whole update, not just that file (the Action token's refusal rejects the entire ref).

Verified end to end on the canary on 2026-08-14 (evidence on #649): the record's write is withheld to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, rides the PR as a reviewable added file, the update parks at `apply-stage`, and a session moves it into `.github/workflows/` byte-for-byte. So `chrome-release-vendoring` should now be expected to deliver when its consumers converge.

**The vocabulary here is stale.** This issue says "baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct" and "baselining materializes it". Baselining was retired in #768 phase 5; the owner is now the pack update flow (`updates/pack-update.mjs`), and the materialize reaches `.github/workflows/` through the withhold lane rather than by direct push — which is precisely why it could not simply be pushed in the first place. Worth rereading step 2 with that substitution before the phase-2 work resumes.

{"number":1347,"title":"Merge the dispatch simulator into the scheduler codebase — the sim becomes a test harness","body":"`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/sim.mjs` (1310 lines) imports **nothing** from the engine: it is a second implementation of the dispatch mechanism beside `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Now that the design is shipped (§17's cadence included), the model no longer runs ahead of the code, so the duplication buys nothing and can drift silently. Fold it: keep the harness, delete the model, and drive the **real** modules from it.

## The drift surface

| sim.mjs | engine |
|---|---|
| `mostRecentAnchor` / `nextAnchor` / `periodMs` / `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` | `queue/anchors.mjs`, `calendar.mjs` (its own comment says "mirroring") |
| `statusOf` + the legacy-label decode | `queue/work-item.mjs` |
| `writeBoardRow` / `boardRow` | `queue/schedule-board.mjs` |
| `schedulerRun()` — four jobs, both occurrence guards, adoption, reclaim | `planSchedulerRun` + the shell in `queue/scheduler-run.mjs` |
| `pickable()`, `claim()`, `postClaimVerify()` | `pickOrder`, `claimWinner`, `conflictsWithEarlierClaim` |
| `janitor()` | `queue/janitor-rules.mjs` |
| `eligible` / `gatedModel` / `APPROVAL_RE` | `built-in-tasks.mjs`'s `APPROVAL_RE`, `parseRequestFields` |

## Why it is feasible

- Every GitHub call in `queue/` goes through one function — `gh(path, { method, body })` from `signals/gh.mjs` — over 19 distinct paths (issues, labels, comments, permission, Actions variables, workflow dispatch).
- A fake GitHub at exactly that seam already exists in `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs` (~45 lines) and already drives the real `runExecutor` end to end.

You are performing GitHub issue triage on the repo `missingbulb/Claudinite`, as one batch of a larger repo-wide "tidy-issues" maintenance pass. This exact procedure ("single-issue-triage") is a checked-in, established skill in this repo used by many prior automated runs — you are fully authorized to close issues, add labels, and post comments per the ladder below. This is real production GitHub state; be precise and conservative per the safeguards below.

## Your batch — triage these issue numbers, each independently, one at a time
1113, 1106, 1073, 748, 722, 1072, 1010, 1078, 394

## Repo access
- Use ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__github__issue_read,mcp__github__issue_write,mcp__github__add_issue_comment" to load the GitHub tools (they are deferred until searched for).
- Use mcp__github__issue_read (method=get, get_comments, get_labels) to read each issue and its full comment history and labels.
- The local checkout at /home/user/Claudinite is a full git clone of this exact repo, checked out precisely at origin/main's current HEAD (commit a06898a). To verify "is X implemented in main" use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash directly against these local files — that IS main's current content, and is faster and more reliable than anything else. Do NOT modify, stage, or commit anything in this checkout — you are only reading it.
- Never touch any pull request. Never push branches or commits, never open a PR. This task writes GitHub issues only (comments, labels, close/open state).
- The labels `quick-win`, `needs-decision`, `blocked` already exist in this repo — just apply them via mcp__github__issue_write's `labels` field, don't try to create them.

## Procedure — run this exactly, per issue, independently

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite the specific file/path/line. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely
looking done or stale. If you can't point to it in the actual tree, **comment, don't close.**

### Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->`, or, on an issue triaged before the
marker existed, by its wording. If the action you are about to take is the one that comment already
announced, **post nothing and change nothing** (a label already on the issue included) and treat the
outcome as `unchanged`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
(where `<action>` is one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win)

If an issue is already closed when you look at it, do nothing to it — report it as `already-closed`.

## Output format

After triaging your whole batch, reply with ONLY these lines, one per issue, no other prose:
`#<n>: <action> — <one-line note>`
where action is one of: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left / unchanged / already-closed

We hit the same wall from the other side (Desktop scheduled tasks, 6 machines), and there is one property of the platform that may unblock you without waiting on Anthropic.

Approvals are stored **on the scheduled task**, not on the run and not on the settings file. The app says so in its own `create_scheduled_task` / `update_scheduled_task` tool result:

> Tool approvals granted during a run are stored on the task and auto-applied to future runs.

So for a prompt that a scheduler cannot click, the workaround is to click it **once, by hand, on a task you then never throw away**:

1. create the routine task once and run it manually ("Run now") with a human present — approve the Workflow opt-in there;
2. from then on never create a fresh task for that job. Re-point the same warm task at new work with `update_scheduled_task(taskId=…, prompt=…, description=…, fireAt=…)`. Measured on our side today: the update path raises no dialog at all, and a one-time task fires immediately (the several-minute dispatch delay applies only to recurring ones);
3. if you worry the reused task shows up under a stale name — have the seed prompt call `set_session_title` on its first turn. Verified: the session then appears under its real name (`titleSource: tool`).

The catch worth knowing before you build on it: it is per-task and invisible. A new task is cold and re-asks for everything, and nothing tells you which of your tasks are cold until one stalls. That part is auditable from disk — each task-spawned session records `scheduledTaskId` and `permissionMode` in `local_.json` next to the task store, so a nightly check can name the tasks that will stall before they do: https://gist.github.com/tonydzi/64183d29eeaa37d7b38a3775012a8c1d (stdlib only, read-only, CC0).

Not a fix for the gate itself — the ask in this issue stays valid. But it may move you from "blocked, waiting on upstream" to "runs unattended, with one human click per task, ever."

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

{"number":1341,"title":"Eliminate the task-janitor: fold its recovery into the scheduler run, its visibility into the dashboard","body":"## The problem

`task-janitor` is the third responsibility of the task machinery (scheduler creates, executor executes, janitor cleans up). Reviewing its four queue rules, none of them earns a daily agentless task of its own: each is either **harmful**, **noise**, or **already someone else's job**.

Owner's verdict, rule by rule:

**A — stale ready** (`ready` for ~2× its period → clear status, park `needs-human:action`)
> So a valid task that just wasn't executed becomes parked?? This seems like it creates more problems than fixes. And the comments are just noise.

The item is *fine*. Nothing is wrong with it except that no executor got to it. Parking it takes a healthy item out of the queue and holds its task's lane, converting a latency symptom into a permanent stop that a human must clear by hand.

**B — dead agent leash** (`agent-running` idle ≥3h → clear status, park `needs-human:decision`)
> The scheduler can identify that and make the status switch.

Structurally identical to the executor-leash reclaim the scheduler run **already** owns as job 3 of `queue/scheduler-run.mjs` — a deterministic, serialized, hourly label rule. There is no judgment in "idle past a clock bound"; it is the same shape, one label name apart, recovering in ~2h instead of ~25h.

**C — stuck dependency** (blocked ≥2 days with blockers open → comment, labels untouched)
> Another noisy comment. The block is there because it's there. No need to make a fuss.

The rule's own comment concedes it: *"Nothing here is stuck mechanically — it will proceed by itself the moment those close."* It changes nothing and posts a comment saying so.

**D — stateless repair** (open item with no state label → park `needs-human:decision`)
> If we can decide on a broken label set — the scheduler can do it by itself and mark `needs-human:failure` and move on.

A torn label swap is a deterministic label condition. `STATUS_NEEDS_HUMAN_FAILURE` already exists in the vocabulary and is the honest classification for it. This also retires the read-then-confirm dance the rule needs today (added for #1104) — a serialized hourly scheduler run does not race the executor the way a daily sweep does.

## Supporting facts

- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/model.mjs` `warningsFor()` **already independently computes all four conditions** as per-item warnings — stale-ready, agent past leash, stuck dependency, `unlabelled`. The broad-scope health review the janitor logs once a day into a run log is a strictly worse version of a surface that is already live and continuous. (Its warning text currently names the janitor; that goes with it.)
- The scheduler run already carries the reclaim machinery (`swapStatus`, the episode-boundary comment guarding against reclaim livelock, F18) that B and D would reuse.

## Proposed end state

1. **Delete** `packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/task-janitor/` and `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/janitor-rules.mjs`, with their tests and catalog/`built-in-tasks` wiring.
2. **B → scheduler run**: extend the existing reclaim job to the agent leash.
3. **D → scheduler run**: a stateless open item gets `needs-human:failure` and nothing else.
4. **A → dropped entirely.** A ready item stays ready; the dashboard already flags it as `serious`.
5. **C → dropped entirely.** The dashboard already carries the warning.
6. **Dashboard**: re-word the warnings that name the janitor to name what actually acts now.
7. **Legacy slot sweep**: `worker.mjs` also sweeps the retired slot mechanism's `[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues still open in members. Decide whether any remain in the fleet; if none, it dies with the task, otherwise it needs a home or a one-shot before deletion.

## Open questions

- Does anything in the fleet still hold open `[claudinite-task]` slot dispatch issues (item 7)?
- Anything that reads the janitor's run-log health line rather than the dashboard?","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1341","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-24T13:33:15Z","updated_at":"2026-08-24T13:33:15Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1317,"title":"Extract the task execution/scheduling surface into a claudinite-tasks pack","body":"Tracking issue for the split of `engine/scheduler/` (52% of core, 8,106 lines) out of the engine and into a canon pack, so the engine is pack distribution only. End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.
- The `pending-workflows/` withhold lane is deleted: after #1302 and #1290 the member workflow files are static (one-time cron at setup, `run:` lines pointing at stable mount pack paths). A structural YAML change is an explicit human-supported fleet PR event.
- A repo without `claudinite-tasks` runs no scheduled work and updates via a human session (update/adopt-pack skills) — no forced auto-update.
- Wire protocol (item titles, labels, run-record lines) is unchanged; legacy `engine/implement-request` titles decode forever.

## Plan

**Phase 0 — out-of-band setup:** none required. No new secret, permission, or platform setting; #1302 already removed the secrets variance.

**Review pass — one PR stack, approved together:**
- [ ] PR A — create `packs/claudinite-tasks/`: move `engine/scheduler/*` in (with `shared-code/`), leave re-export shims at every old `engine/scheduler/*` path a fielded caller names, adjust the vendor set (operational-`.md` whitelist paths, engine walk), move `engine-tests/scheduler/` **and `docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/` (sim.mjs, scenarios.test.mjs, coverage.test.mjs)** into the pack's `test/` (SCENARIOS.md stays in docs/ as the play-through record, its sim links repointed), add the barriers config sanctioning `shared-code/*`.
- [ ] PR B — relocate `task-janitor`, `usage-fold`, and the two task-declaration checks into the pack; `VERSIONS.md` rows in each source pack.
- [ ] PR C — `updates/*` → `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/` with old-path shims; split `converge-wiring`; slim bootstrap (no task wiring); `adopt-pack` scaffolding for claudinite-tasks (workflows, hashed cron, dailyHour, endpoints interview); delete the withhold lane; migration record seeding `claudinite-tasks` into member declarations.
- [ ] PR D (gated tail — written and approved now, merged by chain link L4): delete the old-path shims and any withhold leftovers.

**Execution chain** — each link filed as a sub-issue on approval of this plan, `Blocked-by:` the previous:
- [ ] L1 — force `fleet-baseline` with follow; exit: every member's stamp shows the pack version that ships claudinite-tasks, read from stamps, not run conclusions.
- [ ] L2 — manual fleet pass (owner-supported): repoint each member's two workflow files' `run:` lines and the CCR routine stored-prompt pointers (`executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`) to the mount pack paths; exit: each member's next scheduler run green from the pack path.
- [ ] L3 — observe one full queue cycle fleet-wide (the update task converges through the pack executor); exit: every member's stamp moved after L2.
- [ ] L4 — merge PR D; exit: fleet self-tests green on the shim-free mount.

Deferred by explicit decision: nothing in this plan edits members' `claudinite-ci.yml` (bootstrap-seeded once, member-owned, checks surface — out of scope).","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1317","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"comments":4,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-24T08:55:10Z","updated_at":"2026-08-24T11:44:36Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":true,"sub_issues_summary":{"total":12,"completed":4,"percent_completed":33},"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1333,"title":"claudinite-canary-repo: the withhold lane it probes no longer exists","body":"The `claudinite-canary-repo` pack exists to rehearse one thing: the **withhold lane** — a `.github/workflows/` write diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, carried in a maintenance PR, and moved into place by a session holding a credential the Action token does not have. Its probe workflow, its migration record's revision marker, and its README are all about that route.

#1317 retires the lane. A member's workflow files are static after adoption, so no flow computes or stages one, and nothing delivers a staged file any more. The pack's manifest now says so, but the probe still runs and still bumps a revision nobody reads a conclusion from.

Nothing depends on it, so nothing is urgent. Three shapes it could take:

- **Repurpose the probe.** Have it verify what still matters — that a member's scaffolded workflow files match the stubs `claudinite-tasks` ships, which is now the thing that can silently drift, since a converge cannot correct them.
- **Retire the pack.** Delete it, its record and its stub, and drop it from the catalog. Its premise is gone and a pack that reads as live but proves nothing is worse than none.
- **Leave it.** Cheapest, and wrong in the way the corpus keeps warning about: a mechanism that measures nothing looks identical to one that measures something.

Not decided in #1326 — widening that PR to delete a pack was the wrong place for the call.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1333","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-24T11:22:03Z","updated_at":"2026-08-24T11:22:03Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those

{"number":1174,"title":"fleet-baseline can only force `update` — there is no lever for any other task fleet-wide","body":"`fleet-baseline` is the fleet's only forcing lever, and it hard-codes what it forces:

```js
// packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs
export const FORCED_TASK = 'update';
```

Everything underneath it is already generic — `fireScheduler(gh, fullName, ref, taskId)` takes the id as an argument, and the member-side `planWake` accepts a whitespace/comma-separated list of `task` or `pack/task` ids and *creates* the standing item when one is missing. Only the constant is fixed.

So "force task X across the fleet" has exactly one route today: dispatch each member's `claudinite-scheduler.yml` yourself with `wake: X`. That needs Actions-write on every member, which is the credential `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` exists to hold and which an interactive session scoped to a handful of repos does not have. The alternative — attaching every member to the session — is per-repo manual work, which reliably does not happen.

Surfaced doing #1158's "force `usage-fold` fleet-wide" step. It cost nothing there: the converge `fleet-baseline` forces lands a commit on each member's default branch, and that commit is exactly what `usage-fold`'s movement precondition gates on, so forcing `update` forced the fold one hop later by accident. The next task that wants a fleet-wide force will not be so lucky.

**Shape of the fix** (the lever's `README` already documents the parameter-bag pattern this would join): a `WAKE` context parameter beside the existing `REPOS` / `DRY_RUN` / `INCLUDE_DORMANT`, defaulting to `update` so every existing item keeps its meaning, passed through to `fireScheduler` and named in the run summary. The summary line already reads *"Asked each covered member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` to wake its `update` item"* — it would just stop being a constant.

Two things to get right, both learned the hard way in this repo:

- **The protocol spans repos.** The dispatch input is read by each member's own vendored scheduler stub, so a new spelling has to be one every fielded stub already understands. `wake` itself is unchanged here — only which id travels in it — so this should be safe, but it is the class of change that broke Shepherd's only caller in #929.
- **A parameter that stops being read must fail loudly** (#974). If `WAKE` is added, an item naming a task no declared pack owns must land in the summary's `failed` list, not dispatch `update` silently because the name did not resolve.

Not urgent — nothing is blocked on it — but it is a hole in the fleet's control surface that is invisible until someone needs it.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1174","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-21T15:19:37Z","updated_at":"2026-08-23T18:00:17Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1224,"title":"Eliminate avoidable GitHub-platform assumptions from packs","body":"A census of GitHub-platform assumptions (the platform, not plain git) across the engine and every pack found 367 distinct assumptions counted once per component — 81 in the engine, 286 across the packs.

Scoping this work to the packs, and excluding `git-github` (which owns GitHub as a subject, 38 assumptions), leaves ~248 in scope. Of those, roughly 40–50 are avoidable and fall in two buckets:

**Bucket 1 — not actually GitHub assumptions (~13).** Generic-CI facts phrased in GitHub vocabulary, which the census counts only because the wording names a GitHub feature. They hold on any CI system:

- `firebase` (4) — "release-workflow variables", "workflow dispatch"
- `web-scraping` (3) — runner IP blocks, "repository secrets", commit-step durability
- `macos` (2) — secret-gated signing lane, build annotations
- `spec-driven-product` (2) — CI-gated merge, automated release cut
- `aws-sam` (1) — deploy-workflow staleness caveat
- `research-project` (1) — branch/commit/PR conventions

The fix is a phrasing pass to platform-neutral wording. No behavior changes.

**Bucket 2 — restatements of facts another pack or skill owns (~25–30).** These violate the corpus's own dependency rule ("say what A needs from B; don't re-spell how B does its job"). Repeat offenders:

- "`GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/`" — re-explained in `claudinite-dashboard`, `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`, `claudinite-lifecycle` when the engine's withhold lane owns it
- "`GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes fire no workflows" — re-derived in `claudinite-dashboard`, `chrome-extension`, `static-website` when `git-github` owns it
- the exact-title-tracker / issue-creation-lands-open / no-comment-update-tool cluster — owned by the `unattended-agents` skill, restated in `tidy-repo`, `jwt`, `product-wiki`
- squash-merge evidence rules — owned by `git-github`, restated in `basics` and `tidy-repo` skills

Two exemptions constrain this bucket: vendored workflow stubs must stay self-contained (their comments travel into member repos, where a canon reference dangles), and `task.md` files are read standalone by executor sessions, so some restatement there is deliberate context rather than drift.

**Out of scope.** The remaining ~200 are inherent — the dashboard's rate-limit/OAuth/Pages model, sheepdog's fleet API vocabulary, lifecycle's PR delivery, growth's issue-queue semantics, the two vendored release pipelines, basics' issue→PR lifecycle, tidy-repo's triage primitives. Eliminating those means dropping the capability or building a forge-abstraction seam, neither of which is justified without a second consumer. The per-pack REST-client duplication is likewise deliberate (#959).

{"number":1295,"title":"A member whose Actions jobs cannot start has no escalation path — report-failure dies with everything else","body":"Found while diagnosing why `missingbulb/missingbulbwebsite` had not converged since 2026-08-21 (missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite#217).

## The gap

`claudinite-scheduler.yml`'s `report-failure` job exists so that a scheduled run going red reaches a human — a scheduled run reaches no one otherwise. But it is an ordinary job on an ordinary runner, `needs: [scheduler-run, drain]`, in the same repository as the thing that failed.

So when the failure mode is **"this repo cannot start Actions jobs at all"** — a spending limit, Actions disabled, a runner the repo cannot get — `report-failure` fails for exactly the same reason, in the same ~3 seconds, and files nothing. The louder the breakage, the quieter the escalation.

Observed on `missingbulbwebsite`: ~30 consecutive hourly runs, `scheduler-run` failure + `report-failure` failure + `drain` skipped, no steps, no logs, no issue filed, for over two days. The mount froze on 2026-08-21 and nothing in that repo said a word.

This is not hypothetical elsewhere either — it is the general shape of any escalation that depends on the resource it is reporting the loss of.

## What did notice

Only the fleet enforcer, from **outside** the repo: `fleet-roster`'s drift issue (missingbulb/Shepherd#95), open since 2026-08-20. That is the right instinct — self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence — but a drift issue is a standing report nobody is paged by, and it sat for three days.

Since #1294, `fleet-baseline` now **fails its run** when a dispatched member does not reach canon's versions, which gives that observation teeth for the first time. This issue is about whether the member-side half should stop pretending it can self-report.

## Worth deciding

- Should `report-failure` be dropped from the stub as **structurally unable** to cover the worst failure mode, leaving fleet-side detection (`fleet-roster` + `fleet-baseline`) as the honest single owner of "this member is broken"? It would also thin the workflow further, which #1289 wanted.
- Or should it stay for the failure modes it *can* report (a task that threw, a bad token) while the fleet owns the rest — in which case its own README/comment should say plainly what it cannot catch, so nobody reads a quiet Actions tab as health.
- Either way: should `fleet-roster` escalate a member that has been behind for **N days** differently from one behind by a version — a standing drift issue is clearly not enough signal on its own?

I have not picked one; the first two are a real trade and the third is a policy call.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1295","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-23T15:43:27Z","updated_at":"2026-08-23T15:43:27Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1264,"title":"Delete the two-name settings-file tolerance once no member carries .claudinite-checks.json","body":"Phase 3 of #1252. The rename landed with every reader in the corpus accepting **both** settings-file names, because a member renames its own file only on the converge that carries `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`. This issue is the removal of that tolerance.

## The precondition — a converge-cycle fact, never a date

Do not open this on a calendar. The condition is: **no member still carries `.claudinite-checks.json`**, confirmed by reading the fleet's own artifacts rather than assumed from elapsed time. Retiring a tolerance while a member is still on the old shape does not just leave that member behind — every reader then finds no settings file at all, which reads as "declares no packs, never adopted", silently, with green runs to show for it (the same class as #1106).

The sheepdog roster walk already reads each member's declaration under both names, so the cheapest confirmation is to have it report which name each member answered on.

## What comes out

- `engine/settings-file.mjs`: `LEGACY_SETTINGS_FILE`, and `SETTINGS_FILES` collapses to the one name. Everything downstream that maps over it becomes a single path.
- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`: `LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS` (`claudinite`, `maintenance`) and the two fold-in branches that read them — the legacy `packVersions` map, `claudinite.engineVersion`, and `maintenance.delivery` → `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview`. - `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`: `LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY`, and `SCHEDULE_KEYS` drops `endpoints`.

- `engine/served-by.mjs`: same gate, same walk. Nothing in canon calls it now.
- The both-name reads in `fleet-api.mjs`, `fleet-reads.mjs`, `signals/fleet.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-dashboard/settings-read.mjs`, `seeds-agree.mjs`, `adopt-pack/checks.mjs`, `selftest.mjs`, and the older migration records that read the declaration.
