{"number":840,"title":"Engine-driven format changes to consumer-held files need a first-class migration class","body":"Owner decision context (2026-08-14, on #564): converting members' local `pack.mjs` files to `pack.json` rides a `basics` pack record with `applyStage` — but the owner flagged the routing itself as the gap: *"this is a classic 'engine changed, the format of local packs should change' migration."*

The gap: the **engine** owns the local-pack manifest format, but the engine flow may carry no agentic work (versioned-updates DESIGN §5), and its declarative ops (`aliases`/`materialize`/`rewrite`/`declarePacks`) cannot express "reshape this member-authored file". So every engine-side format change to a consumer-held file gets routed ad-hoc through whichever pack is convenient (`basics`, because it is declared everywhere) — the same shape as the #555 manifest tightening, which shipped with *no* carrier and broke eleven local packs silently.

Ask: make "the engine changed a format consumers hold" a recognized migration class with a designated carrier — so the record can be authored where the change lives (with the engine), while the member-side session it needs runs through the one agentic lane that exists (the pack flow), without each occurrence re-deriving the routing. `legacyPresent` telemetry and the retirement gate should come with the class, not be re-invented per change.

Closing condition: the next engine-owned format change to a consumer-held file has an obvious, documented place to land, and the pack.json conversion's routing (via `basics`) is either retroactively blessed as that place or superseded by it.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/840","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-14T18:43:43Z","updated_at":"2026-08-19T05:18:51Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":996,"title":"dashboard: sign-in is the only route to a usable rate limit — wire it for the fleet deployment","body":"Being logged in to github.com in the browser buys the dashboard nothing: cookies are not sent to `api.github.com` and it refuses cookie auth cross-origin. So an unconfigured deployment runs **unauthenticated at 60 requests/hour per IP**, which one fleet sweep exceeds.

The ceilings, from [GitHub's docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api):

| credential | limit |
|---|---|
| unauthenticated | 60/hr per IP |
| user token (PAT, OAuth, GitHub App user token) | 5,000/hr, shared across every app acting for that user |
| GitHub App installation token | 5,000/hr min, up to 12,500 by fleet size |
| Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` | 1,000/hr per repository |

There is no higher tier available to a page that runs as the viewer — 5,000/hr is the ceiling, and it is 83× what the deployment gets today. **The whole fix is configuring `clientId` + `exchangeUrl`** so the sign-in button exists.

Work:
- register a GitHub App for the deployment, deploy `oauth-exchange.example.mjs`, set both keys on the pack declaration (the manual half needs its own handover issue);
- until then, say so in the page: an anonymous viewer must be told what their 60/hour means and that their github.com session is not a credential.

An installation token would raise the ceiling but needs a backend holding a shared credential — it would show every viewer everything the app can see, which is not the access model this page has.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/996","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["blocked"],"assignees":[],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-18T14:01:16Z","updated_at":"2026-08-19T05:17:01Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1003,"title":"Manual: register this fleet owner's GitHub App and deploy its token exchange","body":"Four steps no Action can take — they need a credential and a console. Until all four are done the dashboard runs **unauthenticated at 60 requests/hour per IP**, which one fleet sweep exceeds. Context in #996.

**Scope: once per fleet *owner*, not once per fleet — and not once for everybody.** One App and one exchange endpoint serve every deployment *you* own. A GitHub App carries [up to 10 callback URLs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app/about-the-user-authorization-callback-url), and with **wildcard matching** a single callback of `https://.github.io/` covers every project Pages site under that host — so a new Shepherd for a new fleet of yours adds no callback at all, just the two config keys.

Somebody else adopting this pack cannot inherit it, for mechanical reasons: a private App "can only be installed on the account that owns the app. Only members of the organization that owns it can authorize it", and even a public one yields a user token that "can only access resources that both the user and app can access" — so until they install it themselves their whole fleet reads *not visible to you*, and their tokens would be minted by someone else's endpoint. They register their own, or use the token box. Spelled out in the pack README (#1007).

- [ ] **Register a GitHub App** ([new App](https://github.com/settings/apps/new)) with read-only **Contents**, **Issues** and **Actions**, and *Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation* enabled. Callback URL: the deployed dashboard's page URL — or the `https://.github.io/` root with **Enable wildcard matching** ticked, which covers every future deployment on that host. Note the **client ID**, generate a **client secret**.
  - *while undone:* no sign-in button exists; every viewer is anonymous.
- [ ] **Install the App** on the account holding the fleet's repos ([installations](https://github.com/settings/installations)). Once per *account*, not per repo — a new repo under an installed account is covered by "all repositories", or added to the selection.
  - *while undone:* sign-in succeeds but the token can read nothing, so every member row reads "not visible to you".
- [ ] **Deploy the exchange** — [`oauth-exchange.example.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/claudinite-dashboard/oauth-exchange.example.mjs) as-is to a worker, with the client ID and secret as its environment. One deployment serves every dashboard you own, since it holds that App's secret and nothing else.
  - *while undone:* clicking sign-in returns to a page that cannot finish, and says the exchange was unreachable.
- [ ] **Set `clientId` and `exchangeUrl`** on the deployment's `claudinite-dashboard` entry in its `.claudinite-checks.json`. Either alone does nothing — the pair is what turns sign-in on. This is the one step a new fleet of yours repeats, with the same two values.
  - *while undone:* nothing changes; the page keeps falling back to the token box.

**Closing condition:** the deployed dashboard shows *Sign in with GitHub*, one authorization gets a viewer through a full fleet sweep, and the rate pill reads `…/5000 · user`.

### Why the exchange cannot be skipped

Verified against the [authorizing-OAuth-apps docs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps):

- the web flow's token exchange lists `client_secret` as **Required**, flatly — GitHub supports PKCE (`code_challenge`, S256 only) but as *additional* protection, not as a public-client mode that drops the secret;
- the device flow genuinely needs no secret ("The `client_secret` is not needed for the device flow") but it POSTs to `github.com/login/device/code` and `github.com/login/oauth/access_token`, and those are cross-origin for a page on `github.io`. The docs state "CORS pre-flight requests (OPTIONS) are not supported at this time"; a browser cannot read a response that carries no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` either. *(The response headers of the token endpoint could not be probed from this sandbox — the proxy denies it — so that last half is documented, not measured here.)*

A browser extension is the case where this *does* work without a server, which is why the Chrome extension flow felt server-free: an extension with host permissions is not subject to the page's CORS rules, so it can call the token endpoint itself. A static page has no such exemption.

{"number":920,"title":"sharedMount's path regex is mount-only, so the signal is dead in the canon home","body":"`engine/scheduler/signals/index.mjs`'s `sharedMount` collector matches vendored pack files as:

```js
/^\.claudinite\/shared\/packs\/([^/]+)\//
```

The canon home runs the same engine from its repo root, where there is no `.claudinite/shared/` and the shared packs are `packs/`. So `changedPacks` is permanently empty here, and every precondition reading it is blind in the one repo whose canon moves every day:

- `grow_with_claudinite/growth-dedup` can only ever wake on its local-packs arm.
- `core/update` loses the "a pack moved" arm of its overdue gate.

The two-root form the local pack's own rule prescribes:

```js
/^(?:\.claudinite\/shared\/)?packs\/([^/]+)\/.+/
```

A local pack (`.claudinite/local/packs/…`, `.claudinite/local_packs/…`) matches neither root, which is the intent.

Split out of #912 / #913, which needed the same discrimination and does it inside the pack (`packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-dedup/worker.mjs`'s `canonPackOf`, with its own tests). Landing it engine-side would let that worker read the shared form instead — worth doing, but it is engine work with two consumers, so it gets its own change rather than riding a pack PR.

- **Forcing ad-hoc work is creating an item**: parameterized runs, `manual`
  tasks, fan-out targets. The CLI/composite (`create-work-item <pack>/<task>
  [--urgent] [--context …] [--supersedes #N]`) writes the generic "forced by
  hand — no precondition asserts there is work" Context; `--supersedes`
  additionally closes a named errored item as superseded by this retry. The
  CLI warns when an open same-title item exists — the pick-time mutex (§6.1)
  means the new item queues behind it, and the operator should know they are
  queueing, not jumping (SCENARIOS S15/F6). `FORCE_TASKS`, the
  forced-verdict path, the `~f` marker and the watermark exclusion all
  reduce to these two levers.
- **Cancelling one executor run means "move on", and the mechanism already
  reads it that way** (owner, 2026-08-16). A single cancellation is
  indistinguishable from a crash: the failure continuation (§10) keeps the
  train moving, and the cancelled run's item is freed by the leash. What a
  single cancellation can *never* mean is "stop the system" — the scheduler run and
  events keep spawning runs — so that intent gets its own lever:
- **Suspending the whole queue is `CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL`** (owner,
  2026-08-16): a repo Actions **variable** (`vars.*`, stamped into each
  workflow's env by the wiring — settable in the UI or over the API, **no
  commit**), which every Claudinite workflow — scheduler run and executor alike —
  checks as its *first act* and, when true, exits cleanly having fired
  nothing. The train parks at most one item after suspension: a fresh start
  sees the variable and exits, and a live drain re-reads it between items
  (an API read — the env copy lands at run start only, §15.30) and stops
  picking. That live read is the one part of the hold whose *reach* depends on
  a grant we have not confirmed: reading a repository variable is scoped to
  the token's variables access, which the workflow `permissions:` block has no
  key for. Where the token cannot make that read, the drain says so on every
  boundary and falls back to the value its run started with — the hold then
  parks *starts* exactly as it did before the drain batched, which is why
  nothing here is load-bearing on the grant. Cancelling the run remains the
  unconditional lever, and the hold is what stops its continuation resuming. Suspension never interrupts *running* work: the current item and
  agent sessions finish on their own — cancel those by hand if the
  hold is urgent — and items freeze exactly where they are, no labels
  touched, which is what makes the hold stateless. This is not dormancy:
  `dormant` is a *declared standing state* in tracked config, a commit,
  read by the same gates; the suspend variable is the instant, out-of-band
  operational hold. (S37.)
- **Resuming is clearing the variable — recovery needs no lever of its own.**
  The next cron scheduler run performs the entire self-heal unaided: its reclaim job
  frees the claims of runs killed during the hold (their heartbeats long
  silent), its readiness job wakes whatever came due, and its drain picks the
  queue back up. An operator who won't wait the ≤1h dispatches the
  **scheduler** workflow by hand — the scheduler run-plus-drain pair, *not* the bare
  executor, whose run would drain ready items but skip the reclaim/ready
  half that makes resume complete. (S38.)
- **`manual` tasks** are simply tasks the scheduler run never instantiates: their items
  are only ever created by hand or by other tasks. The frequency token
  survives; the special-case slot resolution for it dies.
- **Fan-out across repos** is the enforcer creating one item per member repo
  (urgent when the pass is urgent) instead of firing member schedulers with

{"number":926,"title":"The declarative vocabulary has never reached a member's local pack — fleet census, and the one key that is missing","body":"#880 closed the coded→declared question for the **canon**. This is the same question asked of the **fleet**, and the answer is different: the canon is 49/85 declared, and until today every member repo was **0**.

## Census (2026-08-16, each member's `main`, shallow clones)

Local-pack rule modules, excluding `pack.mjs` / `lib.mjs` / task workers / tests:

| repo | local packs | coded rules | declarations |
|---|---|---|---|
| CrosswordChat | 2 | 8 | 0 |
| EdFringeNow | 3 | 7 | 0 |
| VascularColoring | 1 | 7 | 0 |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| Sheepdog | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| gRatio | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| HelloWorldFlutterApp | 1 | 5 | 0 |
| LaughCounter | 3 | 10 → **5** | **2 files, 5 rules** |
| ClaudiniteCanary | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | 1 | 4 | 0 |
| TLDR | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| **total** | **16** | **62 → 57** | **5** |

LaughCounter's column moved today — missingbulb/LaughCounter#203 converts five, the first declarations in any member repo.

## Two members cannot carry a declaration at all

`HelloWorldFlutterApp` and `gRatio` have no `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs` in their mount, so their 10 rules are not a conversion backlog — they are a **convergence** finding. Both last moved 2026-08-12. Worth reading their stamps and the head sha's runs before anything else is proposed for them, per the standing "read the member's own artifacts first" rule.

## The one missing vocabulary key, with two named customers

Every content assertion in the vocabulary predicates on a file's **text**. Two fleet rules assert about a **path's existence alone**:

- `vascular-coloring/rendered-overlays-untracked` — no tracked image under `analysis/`
- `edfringe/no-stray-package-json` — no `package.json` outside the root and a grandfathered `plan/`

`repoWide.flagFilesMatching` matches text, so today these convert only by pairing a path-selecting `scanFiles` with an always-true content regex — a hack that reads as nothing. The honest form is a `forbidPathsMatching` assertion (pattern + exceptions + `what`/`fix`), which is the exact negative of the existing `requirePaths`. Both customers exist now; I'd build it against them rather than speculatively.

## What the rest of the fleet's rules actually are

All 62 were signal-classified (transcript / git / parse / derived-scan-set / config), and ~15 read in full — so treat the per-rule verdicts below as firm and the residue as classified but not individually argued to #880's standard.

The residue falls into the same classes #880 named, and the fleet is if anything *more* weighted to them, because a local pack exists precisely to carry what the canon shelf could not:

- **Derived scan set / derived key set** — the largest group. `shouts-and-whispers/cross-tier-constant-coverage` quantifies over constants discovered in one tier and looks for them in another *and* in the guard's own `PAIRS` map; `canary/pack-shape` reads the skill names out of `pack.mjs` and checks each named file exists.
- **Needs a real parser** — `edfringe-data/normalizer-selftest-in-verify` strips `step "…"` labels out of a shell script before looking for the command, precisely because a grep for the two tokens is satisfied by the label alone.
- **Computation** — `vascular-coloring/overlay-color-contrast` parses `(r, g, b)` literals and asserts `r - g >= 60 && r - b >= 60`. No pattern language expresses that, and it should not try.
- **Imports the definition it guards** — several read a constant or list out of the very code they check, which is the class where coded is the *stronger* rung.

Two near-misses worth naming, both one key from convertible:

- `on-device-privacy/on-device-speech` (LaughCounter) — asserts an opt-out appears within **12 lines after** a construction. `andIndentedBlockBelowMatches` does not fit: the opt-out sits at the same indentation, not inside a block. A "within the next N lines" relation would convert it.
- `macos-audio/swift-toolchain-gate`, `signal-teardown-routing` — both assert **ordering** (a probe sits behind a gate; `SIG_IGN` precedes `resume()`), which the vocabulary has no relation for.

## Suggested order

1. Diagnose the two stale mounts — a member that cannot compile a declaration is the blocking item, and it is not about checks at all.
2. `forbidPathsMatching`, red-first against its two customers, then convert them in their repos.
3. Judge the "within the next N lines" relation on its own merits, with `on-device-speech` as the single customer — one customer may not earn a key, and #880's `matchAnyValueOfSet` is the precedent for declining.

Nothing here proposes converting the residue. The point of the census is the opposite: to have the number, and the reason for each rule that keeps its module.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/926","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-16T11:48:13Z","updated_at":"2026-08-16T11:48:13Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":841,"title":"pack.json migration plan: engine reader + canon conversion, then a versioned fleet migration","body":"Executes #564 (re-evaluated 2026-08-14; PR #569 reviewed for insights and closed). Owner-settled decisions this plan encodes:

- **`pack.schema.json` is authoring tooling** (editor autocomplete + documentation). Manifest conformance — field shapes, the 20-word routing cap, skills↔tree, rule-scope agreement, the accounted-for-`.mjs` guard — is **checked by the world sweep when the file is edited**, not at load. The loader stays minimal and fail-soft: parse, resolve filenames, surface unreadable/unparseable as blocking config findings (as today).
- **`detect` is data for 14 of 17 packs** (path matching + content matching, full-noun-phrase keys per the #789/#799 discipline); sibling `detect.mjs` for chrome-extension, chrome-extension-release, static-website.
- **Members' local packs convert via a `basics` migration record with `applyStage`**; the routing gap that makes `basics` the carrier for an engine-owned format is #840.

Owner approval points: **two PRs** (plus one small telemetry-gated retirement PR later). Everything else lands through the members' own auto-merged update PRs.

## PR 1 — the engine reads pack.json; the whole canon converts

One PR: the reader and the corpus it reads must land transactionally, and the home (no mount, runs repo-root code) is the first consumer either way.

- [ ] `engine/pack_loader/pack.schema.json` — the authoring spec; its field order is the one canonical order (no second list).
- [ ] Registry reads `pack.json`: prefers it where `pack.mjs` coexists (a half-finished conversion must not resolve to the old shape), reports the leftover module for deletion, stamps `manifestFile` so findings name the consumer's actual file. The `pack.mjs` import path stays as the tolerance branch.
- [ ] `detect` spec compiler (tracked-path + file-content matching), with the #569-style equivalence tests: each compiled spec proven to mean exactly what the arrow it replaces meant — including the near-root `maxDepth` semantics and the jwt/web-speech/leaflet content-regex shape.
- [ ] Sibling code files named from the JSON: `detect.mjs` ×3, `env.mjs` where env is a function of config (node; flutter's static shell as data if the spec carries a line list, else a second `env.mjs`), `contributed.mjs` ×2 (barriers, canary-probe); `contributes` becomes a map of pack id → rule filenames; `worldRules`/`workRules` become filename lists (manifest placement stays the scope authority — #555; `declared-checks.json` stays structural with no manifest line — #827).
- [ ] Manifest conformance moves to the world sweep: schema shape, routing word cap, skills↔tree, scope agreement, and the every-`.mjs`-at-pack-root-accounted-for guard. Author each check first and watch it fail (a deliberately broken fixture AND a live in-scope count over the real tree — a path-pattern check that reaches zero files passes silently).
- [ ] Convert all 33 canon manifests + the home's 2 local packs; genuinely unhoused comments move to each pack's README (#569's second commit has the survey).
- [ ] Repoint every `pack.mjs` reader, enumerated from `grep -rl 'pack\.mjs'` in-branch (today: `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs`, sheepdog `fleet-pack-seeds`, `adopt-claudinite` interview, `converge-wiring`, the seededByDefault audit, the pack-prose narration rule, ~20 test fixtures). Fixtures author `pack.json` and copy `engine/pack_loader/` wholesale rather than enumerating its modules.
- [ ] Full suite via `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`; conformance sweep green; both hand-maintained tallies recomputed (not incremented) if checks were added; suite re-run against current `main` immediately before merge.

**Verified in-session**: the home *is* the corpus, so a green selftest + world sweep on the converted tree is a real end-to-end run of the reader — plus one member repo attached read-only to confirm nothing in its (unconverted) mount breaks against canon-side tasks that read packs from a fresh clone.

## Between PRs — the release gate

- [ ] Run the live canary rehearsal against the merged snapshot; watch it to a terminal state (a dispatch is not a result). Note its known blind spot: it drives the worker *this ref ships*, so it cannot see a fielded-caller break — hence the next checkbox.
- [ ] Confirm nothing under `updates/*` (the flow surface fielded workers call) changed shape in PR 1; if anything did, shim per the live-cross-version-API discipline before releasing.

## PR 2 — the release and the fleet migration record, one change

Per `engine/migrations/README.md`, a record lands in the same change as the bump it names:

- [ ] `ENGINE_VERSION` 4 → 5 (the engine that reads pack.json).
- [ ] `basics` version 2 → 3, `minEngineVersion: 5` — the updater's own enforcement guarantees no member converts its local packs before holding the engine that reads the result.
- [ ] `packs/basics/migrations/2026-08-XX-local-pack-json/migration.mjs`:
  - `applyStage: { why, instructions }` — convert this repo's local packs to `pack.json` (+ sibling `.mjs` only where a manifest genuinely holds code), move manifest comments to the pack README, delete `pack.mjs`, repair the member's own pack tests.
  - `legacyPresent` probes every declared local pack (both local-pack roots) for a surviving `pack.mjs` — the fleet census reads it, so "is the fleet done" is telemetry, not memory.
  - `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the pack.json-capable registry **by content, not version stamp** — fail-safe (unreadable mount = not capable), so the record delays instead of wedging (the sheepdog-fleet-baseline lesson).

## Same-session fleet verification — not "after the nightly"

- [ ] Force the fleet baseline/update sweep with `follow`; report per-member results unasked, attaching member repos directly rather than offering to.
- [ ] Drive one member that carries local packs through its update **now**; watch the `applyStage` session convert them and the auto-merged PR land green.
- [ ] Judge freshness by each member's stamp `ref`/engine version, never `updated` alone (held stamps), and read the **status** of every API write, not just its body.
- [ ] Report the `legacyPresent` census: which members still hold a `pack.mjs`, driven by the standing update mechanism — no phase anyone must remember to close.

## Retirement — telemetry-gated, expiry-pinned

- [ ] PR 1 ships a pinned-expiry test on the both-shapes tolerance (re-check at a named engine version), so retirement has a trigger that comes to us.
- [ ] When the census reads clean **from the members' repos, not by reasoning about canon**: one small PR deletes the `pack.mjs` read branch and the legacy fixtures. The record itself stays, as history.

Refs #564. Insight sources: #569 (closed), #827, #555, #798, #768. {"number":409,"title":"Tracking-issue freshness: keep the plan issue in sync after every merge","body":"Implementation tracker for the tracking-issue freshness check. This issue is itself an instance of the pattern it tracks — it carries the live checklist; the committed doc carries the rationale.

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design + plan — [`docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md)

**The problem:** a major task has two artifacts — a source-controlled design/migration plan and a GitHub tracking issue with a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist (the "read status and pick up the work" point). When a phase lands, the committed plan's status is updated in the same PR (the diff forces review), but the issue checklist is a separate surface no diff touches, so it silently drifts. Already live: `per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` says Phase 1 is "same day, no soak" while #394's Phase 1 item still says "Soak ~1 week."

**The design, in two surfaces:**
1. **In-session (timely):** a transcript-only post-merge check-the-work rule — `in-session-github-access` (blocking) means in-session code has no GitHub REST credential, so the rule reads the merge, the tracker discovery, and the post-merge checklist edit from the session transcript's MCP tool calls. Enablers: `work.mergedThisSession()` and a Stop-hook post-merge trigger (the merge recipe leaves a clean tree, which would otherwise fast-exit).
2. **Nightly (convergent):** plans state, per phase, *how completion is decided* — a checklist item may carry `` naming a dependency-free Node script whose **exit 0 means the phase is done** ("if this code passes, phase 3 is done"); no marker ⇒ the phase's prose **Verify** block in the plan doc is the criteria. The `plan-status-update` task (daily, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue) re-derives every tracker's checklist from these verifiers — flipping what sessions missed, flagging (never auto-un-flipping) a checked item whose code verifier now fails.

**Invariant:** any open `plan-tracking` issue must carry a todo checklist and have a box **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it (after the merge, not before — an item isn't done until it's on `main`). The issue *count* is not enforced.

**Phases (detail in the design doc):**
- [ ] **Convention + seed** — define the `plan-tracking` label and its meaning in the `grow_with_claudinite` / merge docs; apply it to existing in-flight tracker(s) (#394).
- [ ] **Primitive + trigger** — `work.mergedThisSession()` (transcript-derived accepted PRs) and the Stop hook's post-merge trigger, each with red-first tests.
- [ ] **Verifier (in-session)** — the `plan-tracking-freshness` rule in `grow_with_claudinite`; fires when a merge happened with no post-merge checklist flip, quiet otherwise.
- [ ] **Recipe wiring** — `merge-to-main` gains the "sync the `plan-tracking` issue after the merge" step (prose asks; the check guarantees).
- [ ] **Docs** — the convention in the pack README; design-doc status box; this issue points at the doc.
- [ ] **Per-phase verifiers (convention)** — `` code verifiers (exit 0 ⇒ done) with prose Verify blocks as fallback; recorded in the pack README and the nightly worker doc.
- [ ] **Nightly status update** — the `plan-status-update` task (daily/sonnet/none, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue): re-verifies each tracker, flips passes, flags regressions in a comment.

**Decisions (resolved with the owner):** label = `plan-tracking`; issue count not enforced; a **checkbox flip** is required (a bare comment isn't enough); label precision from the transcript for the in-session rule; the once-contingent world-scope backstop is **superseded** by the nightly task, which runs with the executor session's MCP credential and has no label blind spot.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/409","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["plan-tracking"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-23T09:56:23Z","updated_at":"2026-07-30T04:45:55Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":498,"title":"scheduler-workflow-shape should validate the scopes a repo's tasks actually need, not a fixed two","body":"Surfaced by the `growth-extract` run on #484, and pulled out of that run's RULES.md entries during review: this reads as a proposed mechanism change rather than a rule a session can follow, so filing it here instead.

## The gap

`packs/basics/scheduler-workflow-shape.mjs` validates exactly two permissions on a repo's `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, both hard-coded:

```
if (!/^\s*contents:\s*write\b/m.test(text))       → flag
if (!/^\s*pull-requests:\s*write\b/m.test(text))  → flag
```

Those two cover baselining's `deliver()` (push a branch, open a PR, arm auto-merge). They cover nothing a *task's worker* needs. So a task whose worker calls a GitHub endpoint requiring some third scope passes the check with a stub that never granted it, and the failure lands at runtime in a member repo.

## How it actually bit (#478)

`store-release`'s worker POSTs a `workflow_dispatch`, which needs `actions: write`. The stub granted `actions: read`. Every fire 403'd, the worker exited 1, and the scheduler converged the task to `needs-human` — leaving three cut-over members with no working release path. Nothing caught it earlier because nothing was looking: the check validates a fixed pair, and the next task needing a fourth scope will land exactly the same way.

## Suggested direction

Make the required scope set *derived* rather than fixed. Roughly:

1. Let a task declare what its worker needs in its `task.mjs` — e.g. `required_scopes: ['actions:write']` — alongside the existing `agent_model` / `expected_outcome` fields, validated by `task-contract.mjs`.
2. Have `scheduler-workflow-shape` union the declared scopes across the repo's enabled tasks with the baselining floor (`contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`) and assert the workflow grants each one, naming the task that needs it in the failure message.
3. Have the stub generator emit the union, so a repo that adopts a task gets the grant with it rather than hand-editing `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.

That turns "read the scope off the endpoint and grant it yourself, and hope you remembered" into a declaration the check enforces. Worth weighing against the simpler option — keep the check fixed but widen the floor to include `actions: write` — which costs a broader default token but no new contract surface.

Not started; opening for a decision on which direction (or neither) before any implementation.

Refs #484, #478","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/498","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-27T18:57:40Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:33:37Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

[{"id":5316661692,"body":"Two more findings from the same adoption, on the owner's instruction to keep them here rather than open separate issues. Both are about **how a human-handover step is written**, so they sit one level up from the path bug above — that one is a wrong address, these are a wrong shape.

## 1. A GitHub settings step must be a deep link, not a breadcrumb trail

The handover issue this adoption produced said things like:

> Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret

Every one of those is a URL the agent already knows how to construct — it has the `owner/repo` — so making the human navigate is pure friction, and a breadcrumb goes stale the moment GitHub reorganizes a settings page while a URL keeps redirecting. The rule the owner asked for: **hyperlink every requested GitHub setting change, to the deepest page that exists.**

The patterns worth naming wherever this lands:

| Step | URL |
|---|---|
| New Actions secret | `https://github.com///settings/secrets/actions/new` |
| Actions secrets and variables | `https://github.com///settings/secrets/actions` |
| Workflow permissions, Actions general | `https://github.com///settings/actions` |
| Auto-merge, merge methods, general | `https://github.com///settings` |
| Branch protection / rulesets | `https://github.com///settings/branches` |
| Environments | `https://github.com///settings/environments` |

This is general to every repo the fleet adopts, not specific to the one that hit it — which is why it is here and not in that repo's local pack.

## 2. Don't ask a human to enable something GitHub enables by default

The same issue carried a checkbox for **Settings → General → "Allow squash merging"**, on the reasoning that the merge recipe squashes always. But GitHub enables all three merge methods on a new repository, so the box could only ever be already-ticked. A handover list whose items are mostly no-ops teaches the reader to skim it, which is exactly the failure mode a handover list exists to prevent.

Worth stating as a rule where the handover shape is defined: **a handover step must name a change from the platform's default.** If the default already satisfies the requirement, the requirement is met and there is nothing to hand over.

Both corrections are applied in the consuming repo's own issue ([missingbulb/Shepherd#3](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/3)) — this is the upstream half, so the next adoption does not repeat either.

One consequence of keeping all three here: this issue's title now names only the first finding. Worth retitling to something like *"bootstrap.md Part 9 path bug, plus two rules for writing human-handover steps"* if it is going to be triaged by title.

2	//
3	// THE THING IT PROVES. `.github/workflows/` is the one directory the nightly update
4	// can never push to: it commits with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which GitHub refuses
5	// under that path, and the refusal rejects the whole ref rather than the one file. The
6	// pack update flow used to answer that with the WITHHOLD lane — every write bound for
7	// `.github/workflows/` diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, staged into the
8	// maintenance PR as an ordinary added file, with the update ending at `apply-stage` until
9	// a session with an MCP credential moved it into place (#649).
10	//
11	// THAT LANE IS RETIRED (#1317). A member's workflow files are static after adoption, so
12	// no flow computes or stages one, and the probe below therefore exercises a delivery
13	// route that no longer exists. The pack is left in place rather than deleted because
14	// what to do with it is a separate call: nothing depends on it, and a member declaring
15	// it gets an inert workflow and a record that can no longer be delivered by machinery.
16	//
17	// That lane had one exercised caller: the scheduler workflow's own convergence. A
18	// RECORD'S `materialize` shares the same `write`, and had never run against a live
19	// member — which is the residual #649 reopened for. This pack is the thing that makes
20	// it runnable: an inert workflow, delivered to a real repo by the real lane, whose
21	// content the canon then changes so the delivery has to happen again.
22	//
23	// WHY A PACK AND NOT A FIXTURE. The lane's failure mode is precisely what a fixture
24	// cannot see — a token's refusal, on a real push, against a real repository. A hermetic
25	// rehearsal proves the staging directory got a file; only a member proves the file
26	// arrives in `.github/workflows/`. So the probe has to be adoptable content that a
27	// member really declares, and adoptable content in this corpus is a pack.
28	//
29	// OPT-IN, AND EXPECTED NOWHERE BUT THE CANARY. `seededByDefault: false` with no
30	// fingerprint, so `--init` never seeds it and no scan ever suspects it: a repo carries
31	// this only because someone declared it. The canary is the intended and only holder —
32	// it is disposable by construction, which is the whole reason the fleet has one.
33	//
34	// THE WORKFLOW IT SHIPS IS INERT BY DESIGN. `workflow_dispatch` and nothing else: no
35	// schedule, no push, no pull_request. What is under test is whether the FILE arrives,
36	// not whether it runs, and a probe that consumed a member's Actions minutes on every
37	// push would be paying for an answer it does not need.
38	//
39	// TWO DELIVERY ROUTES, DELIBERATELY. The `seedOps` entry below puts the workflow in at
40	// ADOPTION — written by the install flow and committed by the adopting session, which
41	// holds a credential the Action token is not. That is the easy half, and it is not the
42	// thing #649 doubted. The hard half arrives with pack version 2 — a record whose
43	// `materialize` re-vendors the same path through the withhold lane.
44	//
45	// THE VERSIONS ARE THE SEQUENCE, not bookkeeping. An install stamps the newest version
46	// and runs no records (`updates/install.mjs`), so a record shipped in the version a repo
47	// adopts at is a record that repo can never reach: `migrationApplies` is `want > have`.
48	// The probe is therefore adopted at version 1, which seeds the file and nothing else,
49	// and the record lands at version 2 so the update flow really has a gap to close. It
50	// also means the record's job is to UPDATE a workflow that is already there — the exact
51	// shape a fleet-wide workflow fix would take.
52	export default {
53	  version: '60824.2',
54	  minEngineVersion: '60822.1',
55	  ruleRoutingGuidance: {
56	    belongs: 'the inert probe workflow the canon delivers to its canary to prove workflow materialization works end to end',
57	    excludes: 'real CI and release workflows — git-github owns workflow practice, each release pack owns its own pipeline',
58	  },
59	  // Not adoptable content: the canary is the only intended holder, so the pack is
60	  // withheld from the catalog every session reads to route a lesson or pick a pack
61	  // to adopt. Declaring it by hand still works — that is how the canary holds it.
62	  hidden: true,
63	  seededByDefault: false,
64	  // Seeded, never converged (the install flow is the only reader of this field): the
65	  // first copy is the member's from the moment it lands. Everything after it is the
66	  // record's business.
67	  seedOps: [
68	    { template: 'stubs/workflows/claudinite-workflow-probe.yml', dest: '.github/workflows/claudinite-workflow-probe.yml' },
69	  ],
70	};

The update 8 commits with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, GitHub refuses that token under that path, and the 9 refusal rejects the **whole ref** — so a single workflow write does not fail one file, it fails 10 the entire converge and everything riding it. #649 is that problem. 11 12 The answer was the **withhold lane** in the pack update flow (retired in #1317): 13 every write bound for `.github/workflows/` is diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, a path 14 the Action token *can* push. It rides the maintenance PR as an ordinary added file — reviewable in 15 the diff, recoverable if nothing else runs — and the update ends at `apply-stage` until a session 16 holding an MCP credential moves it into place. 17 18 That lane shipped with **one** exercised caller: the scheduler workflow's own convergence. A 19 record's `materialize` goes through the same `write`, and had never run against a live member — 20 the residual #649 was reopened for, and the last item left on #768. Proving it needs a record that 21 materializes a workflow into a repo that really runs the update flow, and nothing in the corpus 22 was one. This pack is that. 23 24 ## What it ships 25 26 | | | 27 |---|---| 28 | [`stubs/workflows/claudinite-workflow-probe.yml`](stubs/workflows/claudinite-workflow-probe.yml) | one inert workflow — `workflow_dispatch` only, no schedule, no push | 29 | `seedOps` | seeds that file at **adoption**, written by the install flow and committed by the adopting session | 30 | [`migrations/2026-08-14-workflow-probe-current/`](migrations/2026-08-14-workflow-probe-current/migration.mjs) | from pack version 2 on, re-vendors the same path through the withhold lane | 31 32 The two routes are the point, and their order is the point. Seeding is the easy half — the 33 adopting session holds a credential the Action token does not, so nothing is being tested there. 34 The record is the hard half, and because the file is already present by then, it has to *update* a 35 workflow rather than create one — the exact shape a fleet-wide workflow fix would take. 36 37 ## Who carries it 38 39 `seededByDefault: false`, `detect: null`, `marker: null`. `--init` never seeds it, the fleet's 40 pack scan never suspects it, and a repo carries it only because someone declared it by hand. The 41 intended holder is **the canary** and nothing else: a probe belongs on the repo that exists to be 42 converged against candidate refs and is disposable by construction. 43 44 ## Reading the result 45 46 The workflow's one step echoes a **revision marker**. "The file exists" stops being an assertion 47 once the file has existed since adoption, so a delivery is watched by bumping that line in the 48 template here and checking the member's copy against it. Current marker: **revision 2**. 49 50 A member whose copy reads `revision 2` was reached by the *record*, through the withhold lane — 51 staged into `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, carried in a maintenance PR, and moved into 52 `.github/workflows/` by a session with a credential the Action token does not have. `revision 1` 53 means the seed landed and the record has not run yet. 54

125	9. **Migration notes v2.** A canon change that consumers must be amended for ships as a dated
126	   record (the `<flow>/migrations/<date>-<slug>/` shape): mechanical ops where code can
127	   express them, plus a **brief agentic note** for what it can't (chiefly adapting
128	   consumer-authored `local_packs/` content to a changed engine contract). The nightly applies
129	   the notes dated on or after the day of the repo's stamp (same-day inclusive, note
130	   idempotency absorbing the overlap — #330), oldest first, inside the one transactional commit.
131	   No read-side tolerances in live code, no `LEGACY_*` constants, and **no per-consumer state
132	   held in the canon** — the stamp in each consumer is the only bookkeeping. **Relevance is a
133	   fetch-time window, not a retention window**: records are kept forever, vendoring ships
134	   consumers only the notes landed within the last 7 days, and a repo lagging longer catches up
135	   from the fresh canon clone its baselining fetches, which carries every record. The one surviving two-phase case is
136	   **out-of-repo state** no commit can reach — the pasted web-environment Setup script keeps
137	   the probe + halt-gate pattern ([consumer-safe-changes.md](../consumer-safe-changes.md)).
138	10. **Accepted trade-off.** A bad canon change (typically an overzealous blocking check)
139	    reaches consumers on one nightly and its fix on a later one — up to ~two days' exposure.

This exact procedure ("single-issue-triage") is a checked-in, established skill in this repo used by many prior automated runs — you are fully authorized to close issues, add labels, and post comments per the ladder below. This is real production GitHub state; be precise and conservative per the safeguards below.

## Your batch — triage these issue numbers, each independently, one at a time
1382, 1399, 1050, 1096, 276, 230, 1388, 1324, 1328

## Repo access
- Use ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__github__issue_read,mcp__github__issue_write,mcp__github__add_issue_comment" to load the GitHub tools (they are deferred until searched for).
- Use mcp__github__issue_read (method=get, get_comments, get_labels) to read each issue and its full comment history and labels.
- The local checkout at /home/user/Claudinite is a full git clone of this exact repo, checked out precisely at origin/main's current HEAD (commit a06898a). To verify "is X implemented in main" use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash directly against these local files — that IS main's current content, and is faster and more reliable than anything else. Do NOT modify, stage, or commit anything in this checkout — you are only reading it.
- Never touch any pull request. Never push branches or commits, never open a PR. This task writes GitHub issues only (comments, labels, close/open state).
- The labels `quick-win`, `needs-decision`, `blocked` already exist in this repo — just apply them via mcp__github__issue_write's `labels` field, don't try to create them.

## Procedure — run this exactly, per issue, independently

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite the specific file/path/line. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely
looking done or stale. If you can't point to it in the actual tree, **comment, don't close.**

### Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->`, or, on an issue triaged before the
marker existed, by its wording. If the action you are about to take is the one that comment already
announced, **post nothing and change nothing** (a label already on the issue included) and treat the
outcome as `unchanged`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
(where `<action>` is one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win)

If an issue is already closed when you look at it, do nothing to it — report it as `already-closed`.

## Output format

After triaging your whole batch, reply with ONLY these lines, one per issue, no other prose:
`#<n>: <action> — <one-line note>`
where action is one of: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left / unchanged / already-closed

content.text:
{"number":1475,"title":"Both operational docs name `/scheduler/…`, a path that has not existed since #1326","body":"`executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md` are the whole stored prompt of a member's CCR routine endpoints. Both instruct the session to run commands under `/scheduler/…`, which resolves to nothing since #1326 moved the task surface out of `engine/scheduler/` into `packs/claudinite-tasks/`.

**queue/instructions.md** — the live work-item session's doc — uses `` at three sites and **never defines it**. Since #1326 no definition can be correct: no root satisfies both `/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs` and `/hooks/session-end-command.mjs`. Two of the three are the **terminal transition**, the step the corpus already records going wrong when a session performs it by hand instead (live on #1220, #1265: "hand-fabricating the transition instead is how an item ends up closed wearing a live status").

**executor.md** defines `` as "the parent of the directory this file sits in (this file is `/scheduler/executor.md`)". The file sits at `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md`, so `` is `packs/` and its commands resolve to `packs/scheduler/resolve-dispatch.mjs`, `packs/scheduler/record-exec.mjs`, `packs/hooks/session-end-command.mjs` — none exist, in the canon or in a mount. This doc is the **retired** slot mechanism's, kept for routines not yet repointed, so it is the narrower half of the blast radius.

`git log --follow` shows `a248483` copied both docs `C100` from `engine/scheduler/`. That commit rewrote the stubs' `run:` lines and left the prose naming the old root. No test asserts the command paths; `test/legacy-protocol.mjs` pins `engine/scheduler/…` only as tolerated *input* (a stale member's issue body), not as a command target.

{"number":564,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Owner comment (process-change): "Why are packs declared using mjs? Is it just the `detect` part? It seems they can all be just JSON declarations, and if we have some code that detects, we can put that in a different file. And once it's just JSON — can't you declare the schema in a nicer way than `engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`? You can still have validations (a simple unit test) for making sure all the skills/rules are declared and there's no drift, but at least the files will be sane."

Measured across the 29 manifests (27 canon + the home's 2 local packs): **988 lines, 56 of them `import` statements, 350 of them comments.** Almost nothing in a `pack.mjs` needs to be code.

## What is actually code today

| Field | Packs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `detect` | 13 (14 declare `null`) | ~10 are one-liners over `ctx.tracked` — `includes`, `endsWith`, a path regex, or the shared `hasMarkerNearRoot` helper — all expressible as data. **3 need real logic**: `chrome-extension` (locates the extension manifest), `chrome-extension-release` (recognizes a release orchestrator workflow), `leaflet` (scans file *content*). |
| `worldRules` / `workRules` | all | Code only as *imports*. In JSON these become filenames the loader imports. |
| `env` | 2 | Genuinely code — `setup`/`probe` are functions of the pack's config returning shell. |
| `contributes` / `contributedRules` | 3 / 1 | `contributes` is a map of pack id → rule modules, so filenames. `contributedRules` (barriers only) is a real seam. |
| everything else | — | Pure data: `id`, `badge`, `marker`, `prose`, `seededByDefault`, `requires`, `ruleRoutingGuidance`, `skills`, `questions`. |

## Shape wanted

- `packs//pack.json` for all 29, with `$schema` pointing at a `pack.schema.json`.
- Optional sibling code files, named from the JSON, only where needed: `detect.mjs` (3 packs), `env.mjs` (2), `contributed-rules.mjs` (1).
- Rules referenced **by filename**, which buys a drift guard the current shape cannot have: every rule `.mjs` in the pack directory must appear in exactly one of the two scope lists. Today an undeclared rule module is simply invisible.

## Why it is worth more than tidiness

**The loader stops executing arbitrary code at load.** Today a consumer's local `pack.mjs` is `import()`ed during SessionStart in every session and on every check run — which is precisely why `pack-registry.mjs` carries per-pack import isolation. With JSON, the ~26 packs that need no code execute none.

**A real schema.** `pack.schema.json` gives editor autocomplete and validation that `PACK_FIELDS` never will.

## What it costs

1. **The 350 comment lines have nowhere to go** — and they are real rationale, not noise: why `basics` requires `barriers` and contributes the isolation barrier as manifest data, why `canon-curation`'s declaration cardinality is what makes its tasks central-once. The natural home is the pack README, which is now exactly the "rationale the manifest cannot carry" file after #559 — this brings two or three of the deleted ones back.
2. **`pack.mjs` is a consumer-held shape**, not only ours — every member repo has local packs. Needs both-shapes tolerance plus a baseline migration to retire the old one, per `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

## Scope note on validation

A consumer's local pack must be validated at *their* Stop hook, not this repo's CI, so loader-side validation stays. JSON Schema replaces the **field-shape** half of `pack-schema.mjs`; the **cross-file drift guards** (skills ↔ directory, rules ↔ files) remain loader checks with unit tests over them. Net effect: that module shrinks substantially rather than disappearing.

Follow-up to #559.","state":"closed","state_reason":"not_planned","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/564","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","assignees":[],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-29T16:15:28Z","updated_at":"2026-08-15T08:04:00Z","closed_at":"2026-08-15T08:04:00Z","closed_by":"missingbulb","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":1,"references":[{"number":569,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","state":"CLOSED","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/569","repository":"missingbulb/Claudinite"}]}}

[{"id":5296873425,"body":"**Re-evaluation, 2026-08-14.** The issue was written 2026-07-29; the tree has moved enough that its census, one of its design calls, and its whole "what carries this to consumers" section need restating.

## What changed underneath it

1. **#827 settled the philosophy in this issue's favor, and further.** Declarative checks now live in `declared-checks.json` — JSON, one file per pack, discovered structurally with *no manifest line to keep in sync* — and the format's inability to hold comments was ruled a feature (enforcement by construction). The naming discipline from #789/#799/#800 (full-noun-phrase keys readable cold, no `description`/`doc` crutches) is the vocabulary standard any `detect` spec here must follow.
2. **The manifest vocabulary grew**: `version`/`minEngineVersion` (versioned updates), `seedOps`, validated `questions`, and the #555 split into `worldRules`/`workRules` — this issue predates all of them. Corpus today: **33 canon packs + the home's 2 local packs, 1362 lines, 49 imports**. `detect`: 17 functions / 16 null.
3. **The carrier problem now has real machinery.** When this was filed, "both-shapes tolerance plus a baseline migration" was hand-waving — the standing rule that a tightened member-owned contract must name its carrier came from the #555 incident (11 local packs rewritten by hand). Today: per-pack `migrations/` with version-gated fetch, and `applyStage: { why, instructions }` for member-side agentic work (the engine flow may never be agentic — versioned-updates DESIGN §5). The carrier for members' local `pack.mjs` files is therefore a **`basics` pack record** (declared everywhere, versioned — precedent: `2026-08-13-mechanism-versioned`), with `minEngineVersion` pinning the engine that reads the new shape.

## Revised code census

- **~10 detect functions are path-shaped one-liners** (basename-near-root, `endsWith`, `includes`, path regex) — pure data.
- **3 (jwt, web-speech, leaflet) are one regex over the content of path-filtered files** — also data, with a content-match key; the issue counted leaflet as "real logic" but the shape is uniform across the three.
- **3 genuinely code**: chrome-extension (`findExtensionManifest`), chrome-extension-release and static-website (both read constants out of their own rule modules). Sibling `detect.mjs` for these.
- `env` in 2 (node — functions of per-repo config; flutter), `contributes` in 5, `contributedRules` in 2 (barriers, canary-probe), `seedOps` in several.

## Decisions revised

- **"Rules referenced by filename" is half-superseded.** Declared checks are structural with no manifest line, *by design*. Coded rules should still be filename lists in `pack.json` — manifest placement stays the scope authority (#555), and the lists buy the drift guard: every `.mjs` at the pack root accounted for.
- **Schema enforcement route is the open call.** JSON Schema cannot carry the 20-word routing cap, skills↔tree agreement, or rule-scope agreement — so the code validator (`PACK_FIELDS`) survives in any variant. That argues for `pack.schema.json` as *editor tooling + documentation*, validated against the corpus and against `PACK_FIELDS` by canon-side drift tests, with the code validator remaining the single loader-side authority — rather than shipping a hand-rolled JSON-Schema interpreter in the dependency-free engine (PR #569's route).
- **The 350-comment-lines cost shrank.** #559's READMEs absorbed most of it (#569 measured this); what remains moves in the conversion.
- **Local packs get the versioned-update treatment**: canon converts wholesale (arrives via the ordinary mount converge, transactionally with the engine that reads it); members' local packs convert via the basics record's `applyStage`; the registry's `pack.mjs` tolerance retires when the record's `legacyPresent` telemetry reads clean fleet-wide, with a pinned expiry in a test per the live-cross-version-API discipline.

Migration plan follows as its own issue; PR #569 (built against the 2026-07-29 tree, pre-#555/pre-versions/pre-#827, and carrying the since-retired `agentic` migration field) gets a closing review separately.

{"number":883,"title":"queue engine: implement the work-as-work amendments (heartbeat, tick/drain decoupling, self-re-dispatch, durable record, readiness re-check at close, prework key rename)","body":"The work-as-work review (#876) landed in the design docs and the simulator; `engine/scheduler/queue/` still implements the pre-review contract. - [ ] **Heartbeat comments** — the executor comments on the item every ~15 min during the work step (`prework-run.mjs` / `executor.mjs`); the tick's leash reclaim then measures heartbeat silence. While off: long work is illegal (the leash/timeout arithmetic caps runs under an hour) and items go dark during work.
- [ ] **Retire `timeout-minutes ≤ leash`** in both workflow comments once the heartbeat lands; size run timeouts to `maxItems` × the largest work bound. (DESIGN §6.)
- [ ] **Tick/drain decoupling** — the drain job must leave the cron workflow's `claudinite-tick` concurrency group (own group, or the executor workflow via dispatch). While off: a multi-hour drain starves the hourly tick (F19) — currently masked only by the 50m timeout the heartbeat retires.
- [ ] **Self-re-dispatch** — a drain exiting with ready items left `workflow_dispatch`es the executor workflow (`GITHUB_TOKEN` can fire it). While off: leftover items wait a tick each.
- [ ] **Durable record** — the terminal comment carries the `claudinite-task-exec` record + artifact links (agentless runs especially). While off: an agentless run's only record expires with its Actions log.
- [ ] **Readiness re-check at close (F1)** — executor/agent close paths ready dependents whose `Blocked-by`/`Not-before` now hold, then trigger a drain; tick stays the backstop. While off: chain links wait ~1h each.

{"number":1105,"title":"Engine and pack versions become date-anchored `<day>.<n>`","body":"Closes #1100.

Versions were a plain monotonic counter. It orders releases, which is all the update flows need, but it says nothing about *when* one was cut: a member stamped at `6` against a canon at `13` is behind by an unknown amount of time, and every fleet surface reporting that gap makes a reader go and date it by hand.

Both the engine and every pack now version as `.` — `60820.1`, where the day part is `(year - 2020) * 10000 + month * 100 + day` and the second part is the running number of versions cut that day. Displayed with a leading `v`, as the surfaces already do.

Two decisions worth naming:

- **The year is anchored on 2020, not taken as its last digit.** A last-digit year wraps to `0` in 2030 and sorts a decade of releases underneath every 2029 one. `2026 → 6` either way, so the example holds and the ordering survives.
- **A version is a string.** `60820.10` and `60820.1` are different versions and the same float, so nothing in the corpus may parse one as a number.

### The migration technique

Every reader accepts **both** spellings. A legacy integer parses as `.0`, which sorts below every date-anchored version — exactly where a member that has not re-stamped belongs, so no fleet surface has to special-case it. The tolerance is scheduled for removal in its own change, #1106, once the fleet has converged; the parser's own comment carries that date and issue number.

Legacy integers deliberately stay in two places for now: each pack's `minEngineVersion` floor and every migration record's `version:` range, both of which are references to engine versions that really were plain counters. #1106 retires them.

Zero stays readable and is *not* a legacy version — it is the install floor (DESIGN §3), so `isVersion(0)` is true while `isDeclaredVersion(0)` is false, and a stamp at the floor still reads as "says something" rather than as absence.

### What changed, by folder

- **`engine/`** — `version.mjs` gains the format: `parseVersion`, `compareVersions`, `versionsEqual`, `nextVersion`, `versionDay`, and `VERSION_SOURCE`, the regex fragment the text scrapers share so the six of them cannot disagree about what a version looks like. The helpers live beside the constant rather than in a module of their own, so the engine surface a mount must carry for any of it is one file. `ENGINE_VERSION` becomes `'60820.1'`. `pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs` validates both spellings, and `checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs` reads a record's range and ranges over it through the shared comparator.
- **`updates/`** — the three planners (`engine-update`, `pack-update`, `install`) compare through `versionAbove` instead of `>` and gate on `isVersion` instead of `typeof === 'number'`.
- **`packs/`** — all 33 manifests move to `'60820.1'`. The dashboard's `fleet.mjs` and the sheepdog's `fleet-roster/drift-issues.mjs` scrape and compare through the shared helpers.
- **`.claudinite/local/packs/`** — `pack-version-bumped` and `engine-release-record`, the two canon-side checks that read a version out of a diff, do the same; the first now names `nextVersion(base)` as the remedy rather than `base + 1`.
- **`vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`** — the `versioned-local` shape gains a second local pack carrying the date-anchored spelling. This is the `consumer-safe-change` answer: the manifest vocabulary widened, additively, and the fixture is what proves a consumer-authored manifest still validates in **both** spellings.

`ENGINE_VERSION` moving is an engine release, so it lands with its `RELEASES.md` row citing canary rehearsal [run 32371130795](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32371130795), dispatched against this branch at `1f05d43`.

### One unrelated commit, and why it is here

The second commit fixes `a long work step leaves heartbeats on its own item`, which slept a fixed 40ms against a 5ms beat interval and asserted two beats had arrived. It is red on `origin/main` — three full-suite runs out of four at eight workers — and it was red on this branch's CI twice in a row, so nothing was going to make this PR green without it. The step now polls its own item until the second beat lands, under a 5s ceiling so a heartbeat that never fires stays a failed assertion rather than a hang. It is a separate commit and nothing else in the diff touches the scheduler.

### On delivery

This changes a contract member files carry (the stamp) and the engine flow that reads it, so "will it work on every repo?" is a live question rather than a uniform-by-construction change. Driving Shepherd's `fleet-baseline` with `follow`, and reporting per member, belongs to whoever merges this.

248	## Part 9 — cloud environment setup (Claude Code on the web)
249	
250	The web base image ships no toolchains; installs belong in the environment **image** (built
251	once, snapshotted), not a per-session hook. That field belongs to the container's configuration
252	rather than the checkout, so this is a hand-over step — the owning pack declares it, the script
253	prints it in the HANDOVER block, and the fast path's last step files it. The script to paste is a
254	pack's, not core's —
255	[`packs/README.md`](packs/README.md#environment-requirements) names it and the pack that owns it.
256	Its body is identical for every project: paste it whole into the environment's **Setup script**
257	field and rebuild (`find .claudinite/shared -name environment-setup-command.sh` locates it in a
258	mount). It runs each active pack's declared installs
259	(`env.mjs install`, driven by the declaration); the SessionStart `env.mjs check` then only
260	*probes* and halt-gates on a genuinely missing prerequisite. The network policy must reach what
261	the active packs install from (npm registry, `pub.dev`, …) — the corpus itself is already in the
262	checkout.
263	
264	## Bespoke merge policy (optional)
265	
266	The portable merge recipe ships as the merge skill and needs nothing from you (squash via PR,
267	gate on CI only when the repo has it). Only if your project genuinely diverges: put the policy in
268	its own file and **name it explicitly in your `CLAUDE.md`** — the recipe reads it only then.

This exact procedure ("single-issue-triage") is a checked-in, established skill in this repo used by many prior automated runs — you are fully authorized to close issues, add labels, and post comments per the ladder below. This is real production GitHub state; be precise and conservative per the safeguards below.

## Your batch — triage these issue numbers, each independently, one at a time
334, 590, 840, 996, 1003, 991, 766, 952, 223

## Repo access
- Use ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__github__issue_read,mcp__github__issue_write,mcp__github__add_issue_comment" to load the GitHub tools (they are deferred until searched for).
- Use mcp__github__issue_read (method=get, get_comments, get_labels) to read each issue and its full comment history and labels.
- The local checkout at /home/user/Claudinite is a full git clone of this exact repo, checked out precisely at origin/main's current HEAD (commit a06898a). To verify "is X implemented in main" use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash directly against these local files — that IS main's current content, and is faster and more reliable than anything else. Do NOT modify, stage, or commit anything in this checkout — you are only reading it.
- Never touch any pull request. Never push branches or commits, never open a PR. This task writes GitHub issues only (comments, labels, close/open state).
- The labels `quick-win`, `needs-decision`, `blocked` already exist in this repo — just apply them via mcp__github__issue_write's `labels` field, don't try to create them.

## Procedure — run this exactly, per issue, independently

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**Every checkbox in the issue body ticked** is the author's own claim that the work is done — the
strongest completion signal an issue can carry, and the one thing that puts an otherwise quiet issue
into the first rung. It is **a claim, not proof**: read it as a reason to run the implemented-in-`main`
check, never as the answer. Verified ⇒ close; not ⇒ comment naming what is still missing. A
partially-ticked list is not a completion signal at all — triage the issue as if it carried no boxes.
Where the ask has **no repo-side artifact** (a console setting, a routine only a human can touch), those
ticks by the issue's own author are the closing condition — say so and close.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite the specific file/path/line. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely
looking done or stale. If you can't point to it in the actual tree, **comment, don't close.**

### Never re-post a verdict you already posted

A triage comment updates the issue, and an updated issue is the next window's touched-issue
trigger — so a comment that only restates the last one wakes this task again tomorrow, and again
the day after. The verdict is the news; re-deriving it is not.

Before writing anything, read the issue's comments and find the most recent one this task posted
— by its marker `<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=... -->`, or, on an issue triaged before the
marker existed, by its wording. If the action you are about to take is the one that comment already
announced, **post nothing and change nothing** (a label already on the issue included) and treat the
outcome as `unchanged`. Closing is never a repeat: it changes the issue's state and ends the sequence.

End every comment you post with this marker, alone on the last line:
```
<!-- claudinite:tidy-issues verdict=<action> -->
```
(where `<action>` is one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win)

If an issue is already closed when you look at it, do nothing to it — report it as `already-closed`.

## Output format

After triaging your whole batch, reply with ONLY these lines, one per issue, no other prose:
`#<n>: <action> — <one-line note>`
where action is one of: closed / needs-decision / blocked / quick-win / left / unchanged / already-closed

{"number":1485,"title":"task-declaration-shape passes an unresolvable `automerge` policy, and the task then silently stops being scheduled","body":"`task-declaration-shape` is the blocking world rule that judges a task declaration's shape, and it validates the **value** of every enum field it covers — `frequency` and `agent_model` via `enumField`, `expected_outcome` against `OUTCOMES`. For `automerge` alone it tests only presence:

```js
// packs/claudinite-tasks/worldRules/task-declaration-shape.mjs:66
const hasMayAutomerge = /\bautomerge:\s*/.test(stripComments(text));
```

`hasMayAutomerge` is then used only to pair the field with the ceiling (`pr` without it, `none` with it). Nothing anywhere in the check asks whether the policy *resolves*. A declaration carrying a typo'd rule name, a retired term, or an `under:` scope the member's mount does not yet understand passes the check green.

## The failure that follows is silent, and it is not a parked PR

`discover.mjs` validates for real — `validateTaskDeclaration`, which does call `normalizePolicy` — and drops the task on any problem:

```js
// packs/claudinite-tasks/discover.mjs:67
const problems = validateTaskDeclaration(decl);
if (problems.length) {
  errors.push({ … });
  continue;          // ← the task never reaches `tasks`
}
```

Both consumers render those errors as a bare log line and nothing else — `scheduler-run.mjs:611` and `executor.mjs:630` are each `for (const e of errors) console.log(\`! ${e.what}\`)`. No finding, no work item, no non-zero exit. No world rule reads `discoverTasks()`' errors at all.

So the end state for one bad policy term is: **the task stops running entirely**, with green CI, a green scheduler run, and a single `!` line buried in an Actions log. A task that has quietly left the schedule is indistinguishable from one whose precondition keeps declining.

## Demonstrated

Against `missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite` at `claudinite-tasks` 60830.9, adding one task declaring `automerge: ['under:site/data && typo-not-a-rule-name!!']`:

```
probe task discovered? false
errors: …/task.mjs is not a valid task declaration: "automerge" is not a legal policy:
        "under:site/data && typo-not-a-rule-name!!" is not a policy term …

$ node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
0 blocking, 1 advisory (world scope: all vs origin/main)
```

This was a live near-miss, not a hypothetical. ClaudiniteWebsite#375 landed `automerge: [\`under:${PROMOTED_DIR}\`]` while that member's mount still predated #1474 — `validateTaskDeclaration` returned a problem against the mount as it stood, so the weekly `site-stats` recount would have dropped out of discovery, while `check_the_world.mjs` reported 0 blocking on the branch and in CI. It came right only because the member's mount converged to 60830.9 a few hours later. A member on a slower converge, or a term that never becomes valid, gets no such rescue.

## Two ways to close it, and why I'd pick the second

**Resolve the policy inside `task-declaration-shape`.** Natural, but it fights the check's nature: it is a text scan, deliberately, so it never executes member code. Policies are not reliably literal — canon's own flagship example is now

```js
// packs/product-wiki/tasks/wiki-growth/task.mjs:36
automerge: [`under:${WIKI_ROOT} && doc-changes`],
```

a template literal over a module const, and ClaudiniteWebsite's `site-stats` has the same shape. A static extractor would have to skip exactly the computed cases most likely to drift, so it would pass the very declarations worth catching.

**Surface `discoverTasks()`' errors as findings.** That path already validates with full fidelity — it imports the module, so template literals and consts are resolved — and today its output is thrown away in a log line. One world rule that runs discovery and reports each error turns every class of invalid declaration, `automerge` included, into a blocking finding at author time, and needs no new validation logic. It also closes the same hole for the other fields, since any `validateTaskDeclaration` problem currently disappears the same way.

Worth deciding too whether a scheduler or executor run that dropped a task should exit non-zero, or file a work item, rather than logging past it — a member whose task silently left the schedule has no other signal that anything is wrong.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1485","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"assignees":[],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-30T22:19:19Z","updated_at":"2026-08-31T11:09:54Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":1333,"title":"claudinite-canary-repo: the withhold lane it probes no longer exists","body":"The `claudinite-canary-repo` pack exists to rehearse one thing: the **withhold lane** — a `.github/workflows/` write diverted to `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, carried in a maintenance PR, and moved into place by a session holding a credential the Action token does not have. Its probe workflow, its migration record's revision marker, and its README are all about that route.

#1317 retires the lane. A member's workflow files are static after adoption, so no flow computes or stages one, and nothing delivers a staged file any more. The pack's manifest now says so, but the probe still runs and still bumps a revision nobody reads a conclusion from.

Nothing depends on it, so nothing is urgent. Three shapes it could take:

- **Repurpose the probe.** Have it verify what still matters — that a member's scaffolded workflow files match the stubs `claudinite-tasks` ships, which is now the thing that can silently drift, since a converge cannot correct them.
- **Retire the pack.** Delete it, its record and its stub, and drop it from the catalog. Its premise is gone and a pack that reads as live but proves nothing is worse than none.
- **Leave it.** Cheapest, and wrong in the way the corpus keeps warning about: a mechanism that measures nothing looks identical to one that measures something.
